![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/7fa5e4cd0c573ab5841e3ded221486ee2cabf6e00e1493c3de06fe4d9a87e3a7.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2},$ $y=2x,$ and $y=\frac{(2x+2)}{3},$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,x=\sqrt{2y} \\ y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2} \\ y=\frac{2x+2}{3} & \,⟹\,x=\frac{3y-2}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/63848a26cff0641ac83c73e809028852697212ce64a8cb954815d514922721a1.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{2y}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,\frac{3y-2}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{2y}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{\sqrt{2y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(3y-2)/2}^{\sqrt{2y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
